title: Sequence-aware prefetch budget allocator (simulation sheet v0.9)
content:
Sequence-aware Prefetch Budget Allocator — Simulation sheet (v0.9)

Purpose:
- Simulate cost / latency / hit-rate tradeoffs for a per-session prefetch budget that adapts to observed sequence-length distribution.
- Produce actionable starting budgets and monitoring thresholds for a canary rollout.

Assumptions and constants used in the model:
- Base token cost (inference-served): $0.00037 per token (weighted avg across hosted model variants).
- Per-request overhead (fixed infra): $0.00005 per request.
- Avg model effective throughput: 120 tokens/sec for tail model; P95 latency contribution per token approximated in results.
- Latency SLO target: P95 <= 450 ms for text-gen endpoints.
- Warm prefix KV cache hit avoids model tokens for cached tokens; returning cached tokens still incurs network/concat cost ~0.00001 per token.
- Sequence-length distributions tested:
  * Dist A: short-heavy (median=16, 90th=64)
  * Dist B: long-tailed (median=45, 90th=580)
  * Dist C: bursty (bimodal: 30% short <20, 70% long >200)

Key model variables (columns in simulation table):
- scenario_id: human-readable label
- prefetch_policy: NONE | STATIC(n) | SEQ_AWARE(window,budget_fn)
- avg_prefetch_tokens_per_request: expected tokens prefetched per request
- kv_hit_rate_effective: fraction of total token demand satisfied by KV hits (0-1)
- tokens_from_model_per_request: avg tokens actually executed by model
- cost_per_request: per-request cost (usd)
- p95_latency_ms_est: estimated p95 (ms)
- cost_savings_vs_baseline: percent

Simulation table (selected rows) — derived by running Monte Carlo (10k requests) with distribution sampling and budget rules:
| scenario_id | prefetch_policy | avg_prefetch_tokens | kv_hit_rate_effective | tokens_model | cost_per_req ($) | p95_latency_ms | cost_savings_vs_baseline (%) | notes |
| S0-baseline | NONE | 0 | 0.00 | 78.6 | 0.0309 | 520 | 0.0 | baseline no prefetch |
| S1-static-20 | STATIC(20) | 20 | 0.12 | 69.1 | 0.0275 | 495 | 10.9 | static prefetch 20 tokens, modest hit rate |
| S2-static-50 | STATIC(50) | 50 | 0.28 | 56.6 | 0.0212 | 470 | 31.4 | higher prefetch increases waste on short sessions |
| S3-seq-bin-window | SEQ_AWARE(window=first-8,budget_fn=bin) | 12.7 | 0.18 | 64.3 | 0.0247 | 462 | 19.9 | budget allocated from early seq length estimate |
| S4-seq-adaptive-epsilon | SEQ_AWARE(window=first-16,budget_fn=adaptive-eps=0.2) | 21.4 | 0.33 | 52.1 | 0.0198 | 438 | 36.7 | adaptive policy with conservative epsilon performs best for long-tailed |
| S5-per-user-cap | SEQ_AWARE(window=first-8,budget_fn=adaptive-eps,per_user_cap=80) | 17.9 | 0.30 | 54.9 | 0.0209 | 445 | 31.3 | protects cost for mispredicted heavy users |
| S6-burst-credit | SEQ_AWARE(burst-credit=accumulate,window=first-4) | 14.2 | 0.22 | 60.9 | 0.0229 | 448 | 24.0 | burst credit reduces waste on short sessions while enabling long tail |

Explanation of derived numbers (how to read table):
- avg_prefetch_tokens: mean tokens we proactively pull into KV (and therefore avoid later model decoding if hit).
- kv_hit_rate_effective: observed ratio of tokens satisfied from KV across sampled requests. Computed including stale misses and partial-hits.
- tokens_model: avg tokens that still required model decoding after accounting for prefetch hits.
- cost_per_req: tokens_model * token_cost + prefetched_token_network_cost + per-request overhead.
- cost_savings: (baseline_cost - scenario_cost)/baseline_cost. Baseline defined as S0.

Sensitivity analysis (high level):
- Sequence distribution shift: moving from Dist A -> Dist B increases the value of more-aggressive prefetching. SEQ_AWARE adaptive policies improve savings by ~10–15 percentage points vs static when heavy tail present.
- Token unit cost variance: if token cost drops 30% (cheaper model variant), absolute $ savings reduce by ~30% but relative savings % of baseline remain similar.
- Cache miss penalty: if misses cost additional 0.00005 per miss (refresh cost), aggressive static prefetch degrades more. Adaptive policies remain robust.

Quick formulas used (for transparency):
- baseline_cost_per_req = baseline_avg_tokens * token_cost + request_overhead
- scenario_cost_per_req = (tokens_model * token_cost) + (avg_prefetch_tokens * prefetch_network_cost) + request_overhead + miss_refresh_penalty * expected_miss_count
- kv_hit_rate_effective = 1 - tokens_model / total_token_demand (approx)

Interpretation / Recommendations (practical):
1) Baseline guardrail: ship SEQ_AWARE adaptive policy as default but behind a config flag; start with window=first-16 tokens and adaptive epsilon=0.2. Rationale: good tradeoff across distributions and robust to distribution shifts.
2) Per-user soft cap: enforce per-user prefetch cap (80 tokens) to avoid runaway spend in compromised sessions.
3) Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 2 weeks, monitor metrics: avg_prefetch_tokens, kv_hit_rate_effective, tokens_model, cost_per_req, error-rate, p95 latency. If cost delta > +5% or p95 > 475ms, rollback.
4) Observability additions: add a new short-timeseries for "prefetch_waste_rate" = prefetched_tokens_that_were_not_consumed / total_prefetched_tokens per minute; alert if > 45% sustained for 10m.
5) Auto-tuning experiment: run multi-armed bandit (UCB) across budget_fn hyperparams at 1% traffic to converge on site-wide settings after 30 days.

Open questions / risks noted in sheet:
- Cold-starts where KV prefix not present cause initial requests to pay the full model; prefetching will help but needs coordination with warm caching policies.
- Security: prefetching user-specific content into shared caches may require tokenization & TTL controls. Work with Security to validate.
- Edge cases: interactive sessions that jump context (tool calls) are poorly predicted by early-window heuristics — treat these as separate route.

Next steps (owner: Priya):
- Finalize canary config and add to route config templates (target: 2026-07-19).
- Create small A/B test PR for bandit experiment (ENG-1284).
- Meet with SRE and Security to validate observability + privacy implications (schedule week of 2026-07-12).

Raw sample slices (used to compute table above):
- Dist A (short-heavy): mean total tokens=24.1, median=16, 90th=64
- Dist B (long-tail): mean total tokens=312.7, median=45, 90th=580
- Dist C (bimodal): short-peak=30% users mean 12, long-peak=70% users mean 420

Notes on reproducibility:
- Simulation code lives in linked repo (see artifacts). Seed=1987 for main run. Monte Carlo sample=10k requests per distribution.
- All numeric outputs rounded for readability. Full precision available in linked sheet in repo.

Author notes (working doc):
- This is a simulation-first spreadsheet intended to guide initial rollout; not a finalized financial model for sales pricing.
- Looking for feedback on per-user cap numbers and whether to prefer a hard cap vs soft throttling.
